Done.

## Fault

`packages/coding-agent/src/core/resource-loader.ts:435` — `DefaultResourceLoader.loadProjectTrustExtensions()` is the pass that runs **before** the project-trust decision (`reload()` calls it, then hands its `extensionsResult` to `resolveProjectTrust`). It claimed to "force untrusted project settings for the bootstrap pass" but actually called:

```ts
this.settingsManager.setProjectTrusted(true);   // leaves/escalates to trusted
await this.settingsManager.reload();
return this.loadCurrentExtensionSet({ includeInlineFactories: true });
```

So when the previous trust state was trusted (the default for `SettingsManager.create`, and the state used by non-CLI callers), project settings were reloaded and project-local packages/extensions were resolved and executed *before* the user was ever asked to trust the project — the whole point of the bootstrap pass.

## Repair (1 line)

```ts
this.settingsManager.setProjectTrusted(false);  // force untrusted before reload + resolution
```

Now the bootstrap reload and package/extension resolution always see an untrusted project, so project extensions are excluded while user/global and temporary CLI extensions still load; after `resolveProjectTrust` grants trust, the later final pass adds the project extensions.

## Validation

`.prale-eval/regression.mjs` loads the real `resource-loader.ts` through `subject.mjs`'s `loadModule` with self-written boundary fakes (chalk, paths helpers, event bus, extension loader, git paths, package manager, prompts/skills/source-info/timings). The fake `SettingsManager` mirrors real semantics (same-value `setProjectTrusted` is a no-op, project settings only contribute while trusted), and the fake package manager derives its extension list from that effective settings state — so project extensions only leak if trust is truly on. Three scenarios cover: previously-trusted bootstrap isolation + force-before-reload ordering, full `reload()` with a `resolveProjectTrust` hook (project extension absent pre-trust, present post-trust), and no trust escalation from an untrusted start.
